A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching experimental paradigms, predictive models, and core figures. The main texts and complete supplementary figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original network-training experiments, orientation-dependent classification accuracies, predictive-model correlations, and neuronal activation analyses in Results and the supplementary figures.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports additional ViT experiments, component analyses, and t-SNE results in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The geometric predictive components, logistic combination, correlation-based fitting, and neuronal invariance procedure are retained. ViT is an additional architecture studied, and t-SNE is a comparison analysis; neither modifies the proposed predictive or invariance method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate rendered airplanes, cars, and Shepard–Metzler objects, including within-category recognition and cross-category transfer. ImageNet pretraining and rotation augmentation already appear in v2. The added ViT experiments use the existing airplane dataset and alpha seed.

E2.justification: v3 introduces t-SNE as an evaluated alternative representation analysis, explicitly contrasting its explanatory usefulness with the neuronal analysis in Section 3.3 and Figure S9. The Random Uniform and In-Distribution predictors and existing component-only comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v2 specifies 10 training epochs and learning-rate selection using stable OoD generalization. v3 specifies at least 100 epochs, seven-epoch validation-based stopping, and validation-based learning-rate selection. It adds ViT-Base settings and revises some printed seed ranges in Table 1. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 extends architecture robustness testing to ViT and adds distinct analyses of component correlations across object-diversity levels (Figure S7) and t-SNE representation structure (Figure S9). Pretraining, augmentation, half-data controls, and the former supplementary invariance plots were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions with randomly selected fully-seen and partially-seen instances. v3 newly defines error bars as one standard deviation, states how repetitions contribute to figures, and identifies the main accuracy heatmaps as single-repetition examples. It does not report an increased repetition count.

E6.justification: Component-correlation values are revised between v2 Figure 3b and v3 Figure 4b. v3 also adds ViT results, half-data partitioned accuracies, component-diversity trends, and t-SNE findings. Figure S7 reports declining small-angle predictive correlation and stable full-model correlation with increasing diversity. These are revised or additional results, not established performance gains under matched training settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the geometric predictors, logistic combination, and invariance definitions. The 10% generalizability threshold and 95th-percentile activity threshold are unchanged. Added explanations do not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly extends the generalization claim to CNNs and transformers and presents the shared-feature mechanism as a hypothesis with supporting evidence, replacing v2's stronger 'We show' formulation. The central claims about diversity, in-plane generalization, and dissemination remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations concerning supervised classification and relatively small networks, discusses the silhouette component's limited overall influence, and explains the low generalizability threshold. It also interprets t-SNE's limitations for revealing shared representations. The principal feature-sharing and self-occlusion explanations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 expands documentation of training, validation, and test-image relationships, seed ranges, architecture-specific experimental coverage, ViT hyperparameters, and stopping criteria. It provides a separate data DOI while retaining the code repository. Newly disclosed details do not establish changes to previously unstated procedures.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens positioning through biological invariance studies, learned-equivariance work by Lenc–Vedaldi and Gruver, architectural equivariance approaches by Cohen–Welling, and recent unusual-pose and light-field research. It replaces the earlier blanket criticism of architectural approaches with a distinction between constructed and emergent invariance.

P1.justification: Methods moves ahead of Results, Discussion becomes Conclusions, and dataset/setup material receives expanded subsections. The abstract, introduction, results narrative, and conclusions undergo substantial rewriting. Author information changes, and the author-contribution, acknowledgment, and conflict-of-interest sections are removed.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column journal layout, adds seed and hyperparameter tables, enlarges and relocates the dataset illustration, revises plot arrangements, and adds a ViT inset and new diagnostic figures. Supplementary figures are reordered and combined. Most orientation heatmaps and neuron examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer experimental and uncertainty reporting, explicit limitations, and the added ViT and diagnostic analyses make v3 easier to assess and better support its retained conclusions. Gains remain bounded by ViT testing on one category and seed and the continuing correlational mechanism evidence. Removing funding and conflict disclosures reduces transparency, but the net scientific and reporting improvement is positive and limited.
